title: Gradient sky dome material with sun disc and halo
purpose: Give a three.js scene a stylized sky: a back-faced dome shaded from ground through horizon to zenith colours, a sun disc of a set angular radius with a halo, a CPU mirror of the colour in any direction and a sun angle helper for matching lights and fog. Use it for outdoor scenes and games.

engine.name: webgl2_browser
engine.notes: three.js r155 or later passed in as THREE (the shader includes the colorspace_fragment chunk); only 0.186.1 was run.

contract.language: ECMAScript 2020 module; GLSL ES 3.00 through three.js ShaderMaterial

exports.name: createSkyDomeMaterial
exports.summary: The dome material: back faces, no depth write, no fog; an unknown option throws TypeError.

exports.name: skyColor
exports.summary: CPU mirror: the linear sky colour seen in a direction, sun and halo included.

exports.name: sunDirectionFromAngles
exports.summary: Unit direction for an elevation and an azimuth measured from -Z toward +X.

exports.name: SKY_DOME_DEFAULTS
exports.summary: Frozen default options; colours are linear RGB triples, angles in degrees.

exports.name: SKY_DOME_VERTEX
exports.summary: Vertex stage: direction from the dome centre in world orientation.

exports.name: SKY_DOME_FRAGMENT
exports.summary: Fragment stage: gradient plus sun, tone mapping and output colour space.

options.name: skyExponent
options.meaning: Curve of the gradient above the horizon; below 1 keeps the horizon colour low.

options.name: groundExponent
options.meaning: Curve of the gradient below the horizon.

options.name: horizonSoftness
options.meaning: Half width of the sky-to-ground blend in sine of elevation.

options.name: sunColor
options.meaning: Colour of the disc and halo.

options.name: sunEdgeSoftness
options.meaning: Width of the disc's soft edge.

options.name: sunIntensity
options.meaning: Brightness of the disc; values above 1 suit tone mapping and bloom.

options.name: haloSharpness
options.meaning: Exponent of the halo; higher is tighter.

limits: A stylized gradient, not atmospheric scattering: colours do not change with sun elevation by themselves, there are no clouds, stars or moon, and the halo is a cosine power, not Mie scattering. It does not light the scene: match a DirectionalLight to the sun direction and three.js fog or hemisphere light to the colours yourself. The dome is a mesh, so keep it inside the camera far plane and centred near the camera; it is not an environment map for reflections. Colours are linear RGB triples only. Written for three.js r155 or later; only 0.186.1 was run, in headless Chrome on SwiftShader WebGL 2.
technique_references: Power-curve gradient between horizon and zenith or ground colours
Smoothstep horizon blend in sine of elevation
Sun disc by smoothstep on the cosine of the angle to the sun
